nodes.name: Portal API hostname
nodes.responsibility: Preserves the hostname; health-checked DNS selects Platform first, then healthy IIS fallback.
nodes.description: Proposed automatic DNS failover, requested 2026-09-19. Platform and legacy balancers keep separate public IPs. A DNS health-routing policy selects the primary while healthy and the secondary on primary failure. The authoritative provider and its integration with existing Cloudflare and regional steering must be confirmed; this is not a claim that the policy is deployed. DNS caching delays endpoint changes and existing connections are not transferred. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/traffic-manager-monitoring

nodes.name: Azure Standard Load Balancer
nodes.responsibility: Keeps its public IP as the healthy secondary for automatic DNS failover to IIS.
nodes.description: Remains reachable and health-checked while Platform is primary. IIS must support every route and compatible data behind the failover hostname. This secondary does not accept the dedicated mTLS hostname unless equivalent device authentication is provided.

nodes.name: Platform
nodes.responsibility: Checks approved devices and balances directly across IIS.
nodes.description: Proposed device trust stays inside Platform. Failed checks are rejected; IIS still runs every API. See architecture-design/device-attestation-mtls-proposal.md and platform-migration@strangler-foundation.

nodes.name: Platform Azure Load Balancer

nodes.description: Proposed DNS cutover preserves client hostnames, not a shared public IP. No detach/attach operation is required during failover.

beats.heading: Secure device access
beats.body: Proposed migration: preserve the public address; Platform checks approved devices and balances directly across Windows / IIS. The dedicated hostname and TLS pass-through to Endpoint Gateway preserve original API bytes. Device checks fail closed.

beats.heading: Automatic DNS failover
beats.body: Keep both balancers reachable on separate public IPs. After proving direct IIS balancing, configure health-checked DNS with Platform as primary and the legacy balancer as secondary. Probe application readiness through both paths, test failure and recovery, and account for DNS cache expiry and existing connections. Platform reaches IIS through its fixed Azure outbound IP. Portal affinity must be tested through both entry paths; switching paths may require sign-in again.

beats.heading: Retained operations and prerequisites
beats.body: Direct test access requires explicit controls; IIS monitoring is to be confirmed. This production DNS proposal supersedes the public-IP transfer and manual rollback procedure in the linked engineering foundation. Its test environment details remain evidence, not deployed production failover. Confirm the authoritative DNS provider and interaction with Cloudflare and regional gateways; deploy test IIS applications before exercising failover.

beats.heading: Keep fallback compatible with the whole hostname
beats.body: DNS chooses an endpoint for an entire hostname, not an individual API path. Keep every route and its data compatible on IIS while that hostname can fail over. A Platform-only route needs a compatible secondary or a separate hostname before takeover. The dedicated mTLS hostname stays on the authenticated path; failed device checks never fall back to unauthenticated IIS. Failover is automatic after health detection and DNS cache expiry, not instantaneous connection migration.
